newsitem.title: BELGIUM: RENAULT SEES MANY BUYERS FOR BELGIAN UNIT.
newsitem.headline: RENAULT SEES MANY BUYERS FOR BELGIAN UNIT.

text.p: Renault Industrie Belgium, the Belgian assembly unit of French car maker Renault SA, said on Monday there were plenty of potential foreign buyers for the unit in the town of Vilvoorde, which faces closure in July.

"Paris (Renault headquarters) does not rule out any company for a possible takeover," a Renault spokesman told a hearing on the closure at the regional parliament of Flanders, where the Belgian plant is located.
The spokesman said Chrysler and a number of Japanese and Korean car makers were looking to expand in Europe. He gave no details.
In its February 27 statement on the closure Renault said it would actively look for a car maker which could start up car assembly activities.
Renault is closing the Vilvoorde plant near Brussels as part of a reorganisation of production designed to save it 825 million French francs ($140 million) a year.
The move has angered unions and the federal and regional government, but their outrage will likely do little to cause Renault to reverse its decision.
